public_rationale: Four days before publication, OpenAI's operating chief reported 400 million weekly active users and 33% growth since December. The interview explicitly connected growth to consumer adoption. Those figures contradict complete adoption failure and stagnation under the ordinary usage-based reading. They do not establish profitability or broad willingness to pay.
limitations: Both reports trace to the same company disclosure.
The usage total is not a clean consumer-only series.
The evidence does not settle narrower claims about monetization, retention, or economic value.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Consumer adoption of generative AI has completely failed and appears to be going nowhere fast.

statement.excerpt: The consumer adoption of this software has completely failed, and appears to be going nowhere fast.

from_speaker: appears to be going nowhere fast
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that generative AI has failed to attract substantial ongoing consumer use and shows little current adoption growth.
The surrounding passage identifies ChatGPT as the central example, so its active usage is directly relevant.
Adoption means use; the wording does not restrict adoption to paid subscriptions or profitable customers.
Use February 2025, the current reporting month at publication, restricted to evidence describing the state on or before February 24.
Appears to be qualifies the trend assessment; it is not a conditional antecedent.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous active-use and growth evidence shows negligible or broadly collapsing consumer adoption, including ChatGPT.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Contemporaneous evidence shows substantial recurring use and material growth of a central consumer generative AI product, inconsistent with complete adoption failure and stagnation.
